episode_title: How can I stop treating employee mental health as a problem? Sir Norman Lamb

real_qa.q: What is the main premise of Norman Lamb's book 'Be More Human' regarding workplace mental health?
real_qa.r: The core analysis is that society knows the social causes of mental distress, including workplace issues, but does very little to prevent that distress from happening in the first place. Instead, people are allowed to fall into crisis, and then the system is overwhelmed and routinely fails people. Norman Lamb emphasizes that through his experience as an employment lawyer and later as a health minister, he saw how insufficient training of line managers led people to slip into crisis while employed, eventually falling out of employment and ending up in mental health services—much of which could be prevented through treating people more humanely in the workplace.
real_qa.requete: Be More Human Norman Lamb workplace mental health

real_qa.q: Why does line manager training improve employee wellbeing in the workplace according to evidence?
real_qa.r: There is evidence that training of line managers is one of the best things an organization can do to improve wellbeing in the workplace. Proper training enables managers to get the best out of people by setting high standards while also motivating and encouraging people to give their best, rather than simply complaining, criticizing, and challenging struggling employees. Getting the fundamentals right and providing managers with tools to enable their teams to flourish is at the root of good employment practices, improves productivity, and benefits everyone.
real_qa.requete: line manager training employee wellbeing workplace

real_qa.q: What is Higher Health and how does it address prevention of mental health issues in young people?
real_qa.r: Higher Health is a third sector organization currently being trialled in Greater Manchester with the endorsement of Andy Burnham (now Prime Minister). The program gives young people soft skills essential for the workplace and securing employment, including reliability, empathy, interviewing skills, and how to offer the best of yourself at work, alongside understanding mental health and wellbeing. It combines digital programs with person-to-person learning and targets young people particularly in the NEET (not in education, employment or training) category who may not naturally gain these softer skills through family or school.
real_qa.requete: Higher Health Greater Manchester young people skills

real_qa.q: How does medicalizing normal human responses to difficult work environments fail to address root causes of workplace mental distress?
real_qa.r: When someone is struggling in a toxic office environment—not sleeping and becoming stressed about work—they may visit their GP, who then prescribes antidepressants and potentially takes them out of work for weeks. However, this approach assumes the problem is in the person's brain rather than recognizing that the root cause is outside the person in the office environment. It merely dampens the senses without confronting the actual workplace problem, and people often end up remaining on antidepressants for long periods with potentially worrying side effects, while no one has actually fixed the toxic environment.
real_qa.requete: medicalizing workplace mental health antidepressants toxic environment

real_qa.q: What fiscal incentive did Norman Lamb propose to encourage employers to prioritize employee wellbeing?
real_qa.r: When he chaired a mental health commission in the West Midlands in 2018, Norman Lamb's commission proposed a 'wellbeing premium' where governments could give employers businesses a discount on their national insurance if they demonstrated they were focusing on employee wellbeing in the workplace. The idea is to incentivize rather than assume good behavior will happen naturally, encouraging employers to recognize that treating people properly, training line managers effectively, and behaving well results in more successful companies, improved productivity, and happier staff.
real_qa.requete: wellbeing premium national insurance Norman Lamb

guest.titre: Former Health Minister, Former Liberal Democrat MP
guest.bio_context: Sir Norman Lamb was MP for Norfolk from 2001 to 2019 and served as health minister. He was knighted in 2019 in recognition of his contribution to mental health reform and received the Mind's Making a Difference Award. Before entering parliament, he worked as an employment lawyer, giving him firsthand experience with workplace mental health issues. He has recently published a book titled 'Be More Human: Why Mental Health Care is Broken and What We Can Do to Fix It.'

real_quote: If you treat people well, you tend to get the best out of people. It's not a difficult choice to be made here.
